rule: Each deep dive is anchored on a top-ranked concept and folds in adjacent survivors that the independent scorers themselves said should be run as a SKU/feeder/feature of it. Coverage: every concept that ranks in the top 10 under ANY of the three weightings (the union: 11 ids) is in a deep dive. Constraint check: >=1 T0/T1 (DD1-DD4) and >=1 T2+ (DD5, whose product stage C-22/C-32 is T2).
post_score_kill_rule: Killed at scoring: default total < 55/100 AND not part of any deep-dive bundle (scorers were unanimous 'pass' on these).

deep_dives.title: Memory Lifecycle & Cost Intelligence for OEMs
Memory Efficiency for On-Prem & Self-Hosted Fleets
U.S. Open Memory IP (compiler service -> gain-cell & ReRAM macros)

round2.why: Round-1 red team (05_REDTEAM.md) killed DD1, DD3 and DD4 and downgraded DD2 and DD5 to side lines (0 of 127 objections refuted). That left no PRIMARY-grade venture and no MOONSHOT candidate. Rather than pick from a pool the red team had already gutted, the orchestrator ran a second deep-dive + red-team round on the strongest scored survivors that had not been selected, chosen for the two empty roles.

deep_dives.title: Private MoE Inference Appliance (DRAM instead of HBM)
deep_dives.why_chosen: Highest founder-fit hardware survivor (founder 4/5, cycle 4/5, TTR 10 months, default #15); the only concept that BENEFITS from a DRAM glut; addresses the hottest 'we need more RAM' workload (LLM inference) by using DRAM to do HBM's job.

deep_dives.title: Authorized-Aftermarket Legacy DRAM Die Bank (+ hi-rel MCMs)
deep_dives.why_chosen: Highest ceiling among survivors (Rochester-scale model), moat 4/5 (DFARS authorized-aftermarket status), glut-proof lifecycle demand; the strongest surviving T2+ path after DD5's T2 legs were killed. C-65 (hi-rel MCMs from banked die) folded in as the natural product line.
